news.title: DCC rollback bylaw goes to three regional boards for adoption July 24
news.summary: The Province has approved Metro Vancouver's request to revise its DCC bylaws. The regional district, water district and sewerage district boards all vote July 24; if adopted, 2026 rates revert to 2025 levels the same day, 2027 increases shrink, and the 1% assist factor slips to 2029. No rebates for fees already paid.

news.title: Province extends in-stream DCC protection from 12 to 24 months
news.summary: Regulatory changes announced July 15 double the in-stream protection window for projects facing Metro Vancouver DCC increases, from one year to two. Projects with a precursor application filed before bylaw adoption now have 24 months to reach building permit under the old rates.

news.title: Vancouver unveils ACC program and updated DCL program for Sept 30 start
news.summary: Council reviewed the new Amenity Cost Charge by-law and updated DCL by-law, both taking effect September 30. The ACC has built-in rate increases for four years and isn't expected to be amended until 2030. Applications in stream before Sept 30 get up to five years of protection; after that, a rolling 12-month rate protection applies from each change.

news.title: Six BC jurisdictions have cut development fees in 2026
news.summary: An analysis counts Surrey, Vancouver, Metro Vancouver, Victoria, Port Moody and Kelowna as having cut or proposed cuts to development fees this year, while thirteen GVRD municipalities haven't moved. Stacked savings on a Vancouver multiplex land between 0.4% and 2% of project cost -- meaningful but not enough to make marginal lots viable.

news.title: Builders welcome the Metro Vancouver rollback
news.summary: Industry reaction to the April board decision. Developers describe a narrow two-year window for projects near viability -- likely rentals -- to move, with one estimating the rollback saves $2-2.5M on a typical 30-storey tower. The subdued presale market limits how many projects can respond.

news.title: Board weighs a $389M revenue gap to fund the rollback
news.summary: Staff estimated the rollback would cut $270.5M from water, $75.5M from sewerage and $43M from parkland budgets over 2027-2031. Industry argued the forecast overstates the loss because it assumes development activity that won't materialize at current rates -- Q1 presales across the region totalled 87 units against a decade average near 3,900.
